[Problem]{.card-kicker} **K-th Path** [CF 1196F · K-th Path](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1196/F){rating="2200"}

Sort the edges by weight and keep the first $k$. Call the $k$-th lightest weight $W$. Two consequences, and they are the entire solution:

**The answer is $\le W$.** Each kept edge joins two distinct vertices (no multiple edges: $k$ edges are $k$ distinct pairs), and each such pair has distance at most its own edge weight, at most $W$. That is $k$ distances $\le W$, so the $k$-th smallest is one of them.

**The answer's path uses only kept edges.** Suppose a pair's shortest route climbs over an edge *heavier* than $W$; with positive weights the whole route then costs more than $W$, hence more than the answer — so that pair cannot be the $k$-th one.

Both endpoints of the answer's pair are therefore touched by kept edges. That is the compressed universe: at most $2k = 800$ vertices, down from $2 \cdot 10^5$. Inside it, distances are ordinary shortest paths and can be computed by Floyd–Warshall on the $\le 800$-vertex induced subgraph — $O(k^3)$, no priority queue — which is A1's rank map applied to *vertex ids* instead of values, and A6's "only the coordinates in the input matter" promoted from geometry to graphs.

[Solved in full in @sec-coord-p5-kthpath.]{.card-link}

:::
